d: A weak estrogen made when aromatase converts androstenedione, in granulosa cells before menopause and mainly in fat tissue after it. It is the main estrogen after menopause, so more body fat means more estrone and a higher endometrial cancer risk.
The Stages of Reproductive Aging Workshop system. It divides reproductive life into reproductive, menopausal transition and postmenopausal stages, all anchored to the final menstrual period.
Loss of ovarian function before age 40, with amenorrhea and a high FSH on two occasions. Causes include Turner syndrome, the fragile X premutation, autoimmunity, chemotherapy and radiation.
Hypothalamic neurons that release kisspeptin, neurokinin B and dynorphin. Estrogen restrains them. After menopause they become overactive and signal through NK3 receptors, which causes hot flashes.

The vaginal and urinary symptoms of estrogen loss: dryness, painful intercourse, urgency and recurrent urinary infections. A thin, glycogen-poor epithelium and a rising vaginal pH cause them, and low-dose vaginal estrogen treats them.

Processing of a swallowed drug by the liver before it reaches the general circulation. For oral estrogen it raises clotting factors, triglycerides and binding globulins. Transdermal estradiol avoids it.

Large randomized trials that gave oral conjugated estrogen, with or without medroxyprogesterone, to postmenopausal women aged 50 to 79. They found more stroke and clots and, with the combined regimen, more breast cancer.

Estrogen without a progestogen in a woman with a uterus. It drives continuous endometrial growth, so hyperplasia and endometrial cancer follow. A progestogen turns the lining secretory and prevents this.
The finding that hormone therapy started before age 60, or within 10 years of menopause, carries low absolute risk and good symptom benefit. Starting later raises coronary and stroke risk.
